Article Title: 'Get Harshit Rana and Rinku Singh': Ashwin names Mumbai Indians' ideal Hardik Pandya trade
Article Text:
Hardik Pandya (PTI Photo)

Speculation over Hardik Pandya's future with the Mumbai Indians continues to grow, and former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has weighed in with his own assessment of how a potential blockbuster IPL trade could unfold.Pandya's future has been the subject of intense discussion following another disappointing campaign for Mumbai Indians. Under his leadership, the franchise managed just one playoff appearance in three seasons, while the 2026 edition ended with the five-time champions finishing ninth in the 10-team table.Reports have linked both Chennai Super Kings and Kolkata Knight Riders with a possible move for the India all-rounder. Ashwin believes those two franchises are the frontrunners if Mumbai decide to part ways with their captain, but he also outlined the kind of deal he thinks the franchise should demand.Speaking on his Tamil YouTube channel, Ashwin said Mumbai Indians should only consider doing business with Kolkata Knight Riders if the deal significantly strengthens their own squad."Don't count out Hardik going to a franchise other than CSK or KKR. The talk is that CSK will give Dube and a pacer, while KKR will give away Cameron Green. What happens if Green decides to focus on the Ashes next year? If I were MI, I would accept a deal with KKR on only one condition: getting Harshit Rana and Rinku Singh in return. That is the only way MI gets stronger," Ashwin said.He also pointed out that Mumbai would have to consider not only what they receive in return, but also how much stronger a direct rival could become by signing Pandya."MI will also think about who between CSK and KKR gets stronger through the Hardik trade. If CSK give away Dube and one Indian pacer to get Hardik, they get strong but not invincible. However, if KKR get Hardik, they suddenly look very strong. KKR will become a lethal batting lineup with Hardik. These are teams with five, five and three titles, so MI have to think about how they can ensure one of these teams doesn't leapfrog them," he added.The discussion comes at a time when both franchises linked with Pandya are entering transition phases. Chennai Super Kings recently confirmed the departure of long-serving head coach Stephen Fleming after an 18-year stint, while Kolkata Knight Riders are preparing for life after Ajinkya Rahane's retirement.Pandya's own campaign in IPL 2026 did little to ease scrutiny over his performances. The all-rounder scored 206 runs and claimed four wickets in 10 matches as Mumbai endured one of their poorest seasons in recent years.The 32-year-old has not played competitive cricket since the conclusion of IPL 2026, further fuelling speculation over both his immediate playing future and whether he will continue with Mumbai Indians next season.
Article Summary: Ravichandran ashwin believes chennai super kings and kolkata knight riders are frontrunners if mumbai decide to part ways with captain hardik pandya. The former india spinner also outlined the kind of deal he thinks the franchise should demand. Ashwin said mumbai should only consider doing business with kkr if the deal significantly strengthens their own squad.

Article Title: "He is a great example to all the other guys”: Andy Reid reveals Patrick Mahomes’ extreme rehab routine after knee injury
Article Text:
Andy Reid reveals Patrick Mahomes’ extreme rehab routine after knee injury(Getty)

Why did Andy Reid call Patrick Mahomes a great example for the Chiefs?

Andy Reid reveals Patrick Mahomes spent seven hours a day working inside the Kansas City Chiefs facility

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick Mahomes spent the Kansas City Chiefs offseason inside the team facility, not on vacation. The quarterback dedicated himself to rehab after tearing the ACL and LCL in his left knee, and Andy Reid believes that commitment set the standard for the entire roster.At Chiefs training camp in St. Joseph, Missouri, Reid gave one of the clearest looks yet at how much work Mahomes put into his recovery. The head coach did not focus on statistics or championships. He focused on the daily grind that took place long before the regular season began.During an interview with CBS Sports reporter Evan Washburn at Kansas City Chiefs training camp, Andy Reid explained that Patrick Mahomes approached the recovery process with the same intensity he brings to games.“He just goes. He kept playing, he gets his rehab taken care of before and after practice, you know how he is, he’s all in,” Reid said during the CBS Sports interview.Reid then delivered the quote that became the biggest headline from the interview.“He’s a great example to all the other guys around him that, ‘I’m gonna do whatever I have to do to get myself on the field,’” Reid said.The head coach added that the organization closely monitored Mahomes throughout the recovery.The Chiefs worked with doctors and trainers every step of the way because they understood how competitive their quarterback is.“I’m gonna listen to the doctors, I’m gonna listen to the trainers,” Reid said while discussing the recovery plan and the importance of following medical guidance.Reid also said Mahomes “attacked every day” of the rehab process. That detail is crucial because the recovery did not involve occasional workouts. It became a daily routine built around treatment, strengthening exercises, mobility work and recovery sessions before and after practice.Inside the Chiefs building, players already know Mahomes as the franchise quarterback. Reid’s comments showed that he also views him as a leader whose habits influence younger players. The message from the coaching staff was simple: talent is important, but the work behind the scenes matters just as much.The most striking detail came when Reid described how Mahomes spent his offseason.“He didn’t go anywhere. Seven hours a day, he was there working... and it pays off for him,” Reid said during the training camp interview.According to Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes stayed in Kansas City and built his schedule around recovery work. The rehab included treatment sessions, strengthening exercises, mobility drills and recovery work connected to practice.When Washburn asked whether he appreciated Mahomes’ toughness even more now, Reid brought up Travis Kelce “He had a good teacher with Kelce,” Reid joked. “Kelce was the first one to do it, and you gotta beat him over the head to get him off the football field.”Mahomes entered training camp with questions surrounding his mobility after the knee injury, but the early signs from camp have been encouraging. He has looked comfortable during practice and has moved well during team drills.For a quarterback with three Super Bowl titles, this offseason was not about highlights. Reid’s comments painted a simple picture: Patrick Mahomes stayed in Kansas City, showed up every day and treated rehab like a full-time job.
Article Summary: Andy reid reveals patrick mahomes’ extreme rehab routine after knee injury. Reid reveals mahomes spent seven hours a day working inside the kansas city chiefs facility. The quarterback dedicated himself to rehab after tearing the acl and lcl in his left knee, and reid believes that commitment set the standard for the entire roster.

Article Title: India's day out in Colombo: Shubman Gill sidelined by injury as bowlers find rhythm after sluggish start
Article Text:
Kuldeep Yadav celebrates his second wicket with Ravindra Jadeja and Dhruv Jurel on the opening day. (Photo: BCCI | X)

TimesofIndia.com in Colombo:

Sri Lankan superfan Mohammed Nilam cheering from the sidelines on the opening day of the three-day warm-up match between India and SLC XI. (Photo: Sahil Malhotra)

Brief Scores

SLC XI:

Every time a Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) XI batter hit a boundary, Mohammed Nilam made his presence felt at the Nondescripts Cricket Club (NCC) Ground. The Sri Lankan super fan was in the thick of things throughout the opening day of the three-day warm-up match between India and SLC XI."I remember we met in Delhi during the Test. That Rohit Sharma story of him coming to my home, I remember, my friend," he told TimesofIndia.com on the sidelines.It was a pleasant winter afternoon in December when almost every Indian cricketer, including Virat Kohli, KL Rahul and Ajinkya Rahane, stopped by to greet the cheerful Nilam. His love for Indian cricket remains unwavering, even though his heart beats for Sri Lanka. Dressed in an Indian cricket team training jersey, he cheered enthusiastically for the home side.Right behind him, a handful of NCC members were enjoying their weekend with juices flowing and the music was just loud enough to enhance the ambience. After a humid morning, the conditions became pleasant, making it a very watchable afternoon of cricket.Just like the Colombo weather, the Indian bowlers too found their length in the afternoon session, making the contest between bat and ball gripping.Kuldeep Yadav, in particular, competed with Nilam for the loudest cry in the middle. He had plenty of loud shouts while testing the middle order on a pitch that was hard work for the bowlers. From Mohammed Siraj to Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Ravindra Jadeja, Manav Suthar and Kuldeep, every bowler took time before finding their rhythm. Saransh Jain followed a similar script, becoming the seventh bowler used that day.Strangely, Auqib Nabi, who has joined the team as a replacement for the injured Jasprit Bumrah, didn't get an opportunity to roll his arm over and continued on drinks duty with the rest of the support staff and the net bowlers. The management didn't feel the need to give the J&K bowler a warm-up before the series, indicating the direction they are looking to explore for the upcoming two fixtures.There was rotation behind the stumps too. Rishabh Pant wore the big gloves when the day got underway. Later, Dhruv Jurel replaced him after patrolling a close-in position from the start of the day. It was a nice workout for the bowlers, who navigated the hot and humid afternoon before getting some respite from the gentle breeze in the closing couple of hours of play.The NCC facility, metres away from the venue that will host the second India-Sri Lanka Test later this month, remained mostly deserted for the three-day fixture. Just when India started picking wickets at regular intervals, the area around the members' cafe and the media desk became very busy. A handful of spectators eased onto the railing to watch the final few overs, and their proximity to the biggest names in world cricket kept their smartphones busy.The visitors were dealt a blow when Shubman Gill was ruled out for the day because of an impact injury to his right ring finger during India's practice on Thursday."Captain Shubman Gill sustained an impact injury to his right ring finger during India's practice on Thursday. As a precautionary measure, he will not take the field on Day 1 of the warm-up game against SLC XI. The BCCI Medical Team is monitoring his progress. KL Rahul will lead the team in Gill's absence," the BCCI said in an official statement before the day's play.The opening day of the fixture, where India didn't have an ideal start with their captain not taking the field, was all about volume. The bowlers, Kuldeep in particular, got much-needed overs under their belt and picked up two wickets. SLC XI posted 363 for 8 at stumps. For India, Manav Suthar (2/33), Ravindra Jadeja (2/64), Kuldeep Yadav (2/76) and Gurnoor Brar (1/49) shared the spoils.There was a bit of turn for the spinners as the day progressed, and it will make the second day more enticing when India bat. The onus will again be on Nilam to keep the mood going in front of the members' cafe.363 for 8 after 90 overs (Ravindu Rasantha 71, Nishan Fernando 66, Sonal Dinusha 52; Manav Suthar 2/33, Ravindra Jadeja 2/64, Kuldeep Yadav 2/76 and Gurnoor Brar 1/49).
Article Summary: Sri lankan superfan mohammed nilam made his presence felt at the nondescripts cricket club (ncc) ground. Virat kohli, kl rahul and ajinkya rahane stopped by to greet the cheerful nilam. After a humid morning, conditions became pleasant, making it a very watchable afternoon of cricket.

Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding: 7 football figures fans don’t expect to see at venue ft Lionel Messi
Article Text:

People who are likely to miss out on Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez’ wedding invite

Cristiano Ronaldo and his long-time partner Georgina Rodriguez are reportedly set to get married in Madeira this weekend after being together for nearly a decade. Reports claim the couple have booked a cathedral in Funchal for the ceremony and the luxurious Savoy Palace hotel for the wedding reception. The event is expected to be one of the biggest celebrity weddings of the year.While close friends and family are expected to celebrate with the couple, several famous football personalities may not be on the guest list. Over the years, Ronaldo has had disagreements, public feuds, and competitive rivalries with players, coaches, and pundits. Here is a look at people from Ronaldo’s past and present who are widely considered unlikely to attend the wedding.Cristiano Ronaldo has enjoyed one of the greatest careers in football history. Along the way, he has built strong friendships but has also had several high-profile disputes.Former Manchester United teammate Wayne Rooney is one name that is unlikely to receive an invitation. Their relationship changed after the 2006 FIFA World Cup, when Ronaldo appealed for Rooney to be sent off during England’s match against Portugal. Years later, Rooney questioned Ronaldo’s return to Manchester United.Ronaldo responded by suggesting Rooney was critical because of jealousy and even joked that he looked better than his former teammate.Another famous name is Lionel Messi . Although the two legends have always respected each other’s achievements, they have spent almost two decades competing for football’s biggest honours. Their rivalry has defined an era, but they have never been close friends. With Messi winning more Ballon d’Or awards and lifting the FIFA World Cup, many believe he is unlikely to be part of Ronaldo’s wedding celebrations.Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag also appears unlikely to attend. Their relationship broke down during Ronaldo’s second spell at Old Trafford after disagreements over playing time. Ronaldo later said he had lost respect for the Dutch coach, and both sides eventually agreed to end his contract.Interim Manchester United manager Ralf Rangnick also had a difficult relationship with Ronaldo. Reports at the time suggested Ronaldo was unhappy with Rangnick’s tactical approach and questioned his appointment.Former England striker Gary Lineker has often said he believes Messi is the greatest footballer ever. According to Lineker, Ronaldo stopped following him on social media after those comments. Lineker later explained that he had simply shared his honest football opinion rather than trying to offend Ronaldo.Former Real Madrid forward Antonio Cassano repeatedly criticised Ronaldo during his Juventus years, describing him as an individual player who struggled to fit into a team system. Cassano later revealed that Ronaldo contacted him directly, highlighting his achievements and asking for greater respect.Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter completes the list. In 2013, Blatter jokingly suggested Ronaldo spent more time on his appearance than Messi. Ronaldo publicly shared the remarks, leading Blatter to apologise to both the Portuguese star and Real Madrid. Even so, the incident remains one of the most talked-about moments in their relationship.
Article Summary: Cristiano ronaldo and georgina rodriguez are reportedly set to get married in madeira this weekend. Reports claim the couple have booked a cathedral in funchal for the ceremony and the luxurious savoy palace hotel for the wedding reception.

Article Title: 'Replied with his bat': Shikhar Dhawan throws support behind Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli for 2027 World Cup
Article Text:
Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma

Former India opener Shikhar Dhawan has backed Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli to play in the 2027 ODI World Cup, saying the two will continue to add value to the Indian team and help it compete for the title.Now playing only ODI cricket, Rohit and Kohli had a productive series against England in July, despite India losing the three-match series 2-1.Questions have continued over whether 39-year-old Rohit and 37-year-old Kohli will be part of India's squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup because of their age. But both have continued to answer those doubts with their performances. Kohli scored two half-centuries in the series against England, while Rohit hit a century at Lord's.Speaking to news agency ANI, Dhawan said both Rohit and Kohli have been serving Indian cricket for many years and remain important to the team. He added that he has known both players since they were around 16 years old.Dhawan praised Rohit for bouncing back with a century at Lord's, saying the opener responded to a difficult phase with his bat and has been doing that throughout his career.He also praised Kohli's fitness and consistency, saying words are never enough to describe his achievements. Dhawan said he is confident that both players will continue to make a big contribution and help India in the 2027 World Cup."They are legends, they have performed for the country for so many years. Whether it's Virat or Rohit, all of us have had a relationship since we were around 16 years old. They are 2-3 years younger than me. And it's a matter of great joy that they are preparing now. Rohit recently scored a hundred at Lord's, so he scored a wonderful century and showed how his bat talks. Well, he's been showing it for so many years. And when a bit of a tough situation came, he replied with his bat," Dhawan said."And as for Virat, the more he is praised, the less it is. Keeping himself so fit, performing so well. And I'm sure that both of them will add a lot of value in the World Cup and help the team win," Dhawan added.

Real Madrid have ended months of uncertainty surrounding Vinicius Jr's future by tying the Brazilian forward to a new long-term contract until June 30, 2032. Having joined Madrid from Flamengo in 2018 after turning 18, the Brazilian has evolved from a promising teenager into one of world football's elite attackers. Over eight seasons, he has made 375 appearances, scored 128 goalsVinicius has played a central role in one of the most successful periods in the club's recent history. His trophy cabinet with Real Madrid includes:Perhaps his defining moments came in the Champions League, where he scored in both the 2022 final in Paris and the 2024 final in London, helping Real Madrid lift their 14th and 15th European crowns.Vinicius' performances have also earned global recognition. His list of individual honours includes:He has also been named in the FIFA World XI (2024), the FIFA FIFPro World11 twice (2023 and 2024), and the UEFA Champions League Team of the Season on three occasions.The extension reinforces Real Madrid's long-term sporting vision as the club continues building its attack around Vinicius. The Brazilian is expected to spearhead Madrid's frontline alongside Kylian Mbappe, Bernardo Silva and Diomande as Los Blancos prepare for the new campaign.

Myles Garrett's return to the Los Angeles Rams' training camp brought relief after several days away with a lower-body issue. But just as concerns around the star pass rusher began to ease, attention shifted to his girlfriend, Olympic snowboarding champion Chloe Kim, who revealed she is dealing with a painful injury of her own. Her candid social media update quickly drew concern from fans, especially after she explained the temporary effects of a medical procedure during her recovery.Kim gave followers a glimpse into her condition by posting a mirror selfie on Instagram showing her arm secured in a shoulder immobilizer. The image was followed by a video in which she spoke openly about the challenges she experienced after receiving treatment.The three-time Olympic gold medalist explained that doctors administered a nerve blocker in her neck to help manage pain after her injury. While the treatment was intended to aid recovery, it temporarily limited movement in her hand, something she admitted was unsettling."I wasn’t able to move my fingers, which will last hours because they put a nerve blocker in my neck, by the way. Anyways, it's coming back."Her update reassured fans that sensation was gradually returning, but the video still highlighted the physical challenges she is currently facing.Kim did not disclose exactly how the injury occurred or whether it will affect her future training schedule.The snowboard star has remained active on social media throughout the offseason, often sharing moments from her personal life and interacting with fans. Her latest post, however, struck a more serious tone as she documented a difficult stage of her recovery.Kim's health update came just as Garrett resumed practice with the Rams after missing four consecutive days. Head coach Sean McVay explained that the defensive end had been dealing with "little soreness in his lower half," prompting the team to take a cautious approach before clearing him to return.Garrett's comeback is encouraging news for Los Angeles as preparations for the new NFL season continue. Laughing off the rumors in another TikTok video, she made it clear she had nothing to do with the blockbuster trade."I’ve been giggling at these rumors the last couple of days because you guys are giving me TOO MUCH CREDIT.”The couple has enjoyed a busy offseason together, making their red carpet debut at the 2026 ESPYs and later sharing highlights from a vacation in Greece. While Garrett now appears ready to focus fully on football, Kim's latest update serves as a reminder that recovery can be just as demanding away from the playing field. Fans will now be hoping that both athletes return to full health as they prepare for their respective seasons.

Article Title: 'He's like me, but better': Brendon McCullum's verdict on England's new Test coach Stephen Fleming
Article Text:
Brendon McCullum and Stephen Fleming (Agency Image)

England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum has thrown his weight behind the England and Wales Cricket Board's decision to hand Joe Root the Test captaincy once again, insisting Harry Brook 's opportunity to lead the side in the longest format will arrive in due course.The ECB's decision to bring Root back as Test captain after Ben Stokes' retirement came as a surprise, with many expecting vice-captain Brook to take over. Brook has already been leading England's white-ball sides and was widely regarded as the frontrunner to succeed Stokes.However, McCullum believes England have made the right call by opting for Root's experience while continuing to groom Brook for the future."Everyone knows the affection that I have for Harry," white-ball head coach McCullum told Sky Sports. "He's a wonderful player and he's doing a fine job as white-ball leader. I think his time will come in the Test job."McCullum said England would continue investing in Brook's leadership development, adding that the 27-year-old remains central to the team's long-term plans."I'm looking forward to working with him and hopefully growing and developing him into the leader that he can become.At some stage in the future, he will have a very important role in that capacity. But for now, Joe will do an amazing job," he added.Root's return marks a dramatic twist in England's leadership story. His first spell as Test captain ended amid mounting criticism before Ben Stokes replaced him, but following Stokes' retirement, the ECB has turned back to its most prolific Test batter to guide the side through a new era.The leadership reshuffle has also extended to the coaching setup. McCullum has stepped down as England's Test coach, with former Chennai Super Kings head coach Stephen Fleming taking charge of the red-ball side.McCullum believes England could not have found a better successor, describing Fleming as an outstanding appointment."I had a great time in my four years but now it's going in a different direction, I think Flem (Fleming) will be excellent. He's a little bit like me, but better – that's how I would sum him up. He'll do a great job, and the ECB have done incredibly well to get someone like him to commit to English cricket for the period that he has. It's an outstanding achievement," McCullum said.
Article Summary: Brendon mccullum backs joe root to succeed ben stokes as test captain. England white-ball head coach says harry brook's time will come in the test job. Mccullum has stepped down as england's test coach, with stephen fleming taking charge of red-ball side.

Bangladesh all-rounder Shakib Al Hasan is ready to return home after two years in exile, face trial in the cases against him, including a murder charge, and play a farewell series if the government guarantees his safety, news agency Reuters reported.Shakib, a former lawmaker from former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League, has been living in the United States since Hasina's government was removed in a student-led uprising in August 2024.The 39-year-old has not retired from international cricket and said he still hopes to play one final series for Bangladesh at home before representing the country at the 2027 ODI World Cup.Shakib's situation reflects the wider impact of Hasina's removal from power, with several of her political allies facing criminal cases and remaining outside Bangladesh. The lasting legacy of the Tkachuk family in American hockey

Family Member Greatest Contributions Keith Tkachuk Hall of Fame career, 538 NHL goals, Team USA pioneer, established the family legacy Matthew Tkachuk Florida Panthers star, Stanley Cup champion, elite power forward, Team USA standout Brady Tkachuk Former Ottawa Senators captain, Florida Panthers forward, respected NHL leader Combined Legacy Multi-generational NHL excellence, leadership, championships and continued influence on American hockey

Few families in the United States have had as much of an impact on the modern game of hockey as the Tkachuk family. The family name has become synonymous with elite talent, fierce competitiveness and leadership over three generations of impact, starting with Keith Tkachuk and continuing with his sons Matthew Tkachuk and Brady Tkachuk. Their story isn’t just statistics or championships, but building a culture that blends ability with physicality, accountability and love for the game.Keith Tkachuk blazed a trail with an amazing 18-season NHL career that made him one of the greatest American-born power forwards in league history. The legacy has been lifted even higher by Matthew Tkachuk of the Florida Panthers and Brady Tkachuk, who followed his brother to Florida after making his mark as captain of the Ottawa Senators. The trio has helped redefine what American hockey players can do at the NHL and international levels.Keith Tkachuk was already one of the NHL's premier power forwards long before Matthew and Brady were household names. Big Walt, as he was known, added elite offensive production, toughness, consistency and leadership to an 18-season NHL career.Keith spent his entire career with the Winnipeg Jets, Phoenix Coyotes, St.Louis Blues and Atlanta Thrashers. In the 1996-97 season, he became the first American-born player to lead the NHL in goals, a sign of the growing influence of American players in a league long dominated by Canadian talent.Keith may not have done the most for hockey by scoring 538 goals, but rather by the environment he provided for Matthew and Brady growing up.Like many former professional athletes, Keith never put huge expectations on his children and always stressed the enjoyment of the game. Hockey was still something to get excited about, not something to press for, and it gave both sons a chance to develop naturally, while preserving their love for competition.Hell was to pay in the Tkachuk household. Whether playing hockey in the driveway, competing in backyard games or watching NHL contests together, each activity was a learning opportunity. Keith encouraged both boys to compete against each other but also respect their teammates and the opposition.Communication was also a defining strength of the family. Keith taught hockey IQ, preparation and accountability through everyday conversations, not long lectures. That showed later in Matthew’s emotional leadership and Brady’s ability to inspire teammates.Keith also made certain that his sons knew that talent alone would never guarantee success. Hard work, consistency and resilience were non-negotiable values throughout their development.Matt Tkachuk stepped onto the professional hockey scene loaded with expectations, as the son of one of the greatest NHL players in American history. Rather than getting bogged down in those comparisons, he quickly established himself as one of the league’s top power forwards.The Calgary Flames picked Matthew sixth overall in the 2016 NHL Draft, and he quickly showed the scoring touch, creativity and physical edge that had become synonymous with the Tkachuk name. Everything changed when he was traded to the Florida Panthers in 2022. Matthew quickly became the heart and soul of the Panthers, helping turn the franchise into a perennial Stanley Cup contender.While Matthew may have gotten to the NHL first, Brady Tkachuk quickly demonstrated that he possessed many of the same qualities that paved the way for his father and older brother’s success. Drafted fourth overall by the Ottawa Senators in the 2018 NHL Draft, Brady quickly established himself as one of the league’s most fearless young forwards.Those leadership qualities paid off in November 2021 when Brady was named the 10th captain in Ottawa Senators franchise history. Only 22 years old, he was handed the reins to guide one of the NHL’s youngest rosters through a tough time. His teammates often praised his consistency, accountability and desire to lead by example, not just talk.Brady’s offence just kept getting better, too. Multiple 30-goal seasons and career-best point totals made him more than just a physical forward. Brady, like his father and brother, proved that toughness and elite offensive talent could be found in the same player.His next trade to the Florida Panthers brought the Tkachuk brothers back together at the NHL level for one of hockey’s most compelling storylines. The two became teammates, fulfilling a childhood dream, and giving the Panthers two of the league’s most competitive power forwards on the same roster.There have been plenty of famous family names in pro hockey, but few have built a legacy quite like the Tkachuks. Their impact goes beyond championships, statistics or Hall of Fame recognition. The consistency with which they’ve embraced the same core values while adapting to different eras of the sport is what really separates each generation.Keith offered a physical play blueprint that did not compromise offensive excellence. While many enforcers didn’t offer much offensively, Keith was one of the NHL’s toughest competitors and always ranked among the league’s top scorers. Matthew and Brady built on those concepts, showing that a player with elite skill and relentless competitive fire can thrive even in the faster, more modern NHL.The Tkachuk family has become one of the defining stories of modern American hockey. Keith’s Hall of Fame career laid the groundwork, but Matthew and Brady have made sure the family name continues to grow with each passing season.Their successes have helped redefine the image of American-born NHL players. Past generations have had to fight the stereotypes that the European or Canadian players were better skilled, while the Americans were more athletic and physical. The Tkachuks have shown that elite offensive production, hockey IQ and toughness can all co-exist at the highest level.
Article Summary: The tkachuk family is synonymous with elite talent, fierce competitiveness and leadership. The family name has been lifted even higher by sons matthew and brady. The trio has helped redefine what american players can do at the nhl and international levels. The tkachuk family has become one of the defining stories of modern american hockey.

Article Title: Exiled Bangladeshi cricket star Shakib Al Hasan willing to return, face murder trial if safety assured
Article Text:
Bangladesh cricket star Shakib Al Hasan, an exiled ally of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina, says he is ready to return home and face trial on murder charges if the government guarantees his security.

Bangladesh cricket Shakib Al Hasan has said he is willing to return home and face criminal proceedings against him if the government guarantees his safety, according to an exclusive interview with Reuters.Shakib has been living in exile in the United States since former prime minister Sheikh Hasina was ousted in a student-led uprising in August 2024. The former Bangladesh captain, who was also an Awami League lawmaker under Hasina, has not returned home since.“If I get the clearance from the government that my security will be ensured, I am happy to go back, face the court trial and everything that's needed to be done,” Shakib told Reuters by phone from Sri Lanka.He said he believed the allegations against him were baseless and wanted the opportunity to return and defend himself in court. Shakib said he was also keen to speak with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman about his return.Shakib is facing two active cases in Bangladesh. One concerns the alleged killing of a protester during the 2024 uprising, while another was filed by anti-corruption authorities. He said the murder case was filed on a day when he was playing a match in Toronto.Shakib also said his bank accounts had been frozen for around 18 months while investigations continued. He has not appointed a defence lawyer in the murder case, according to Reuters.His political links remain a major obstacle to his return. Shakib defended his decision to appear virtually at a press conference with Hasina in Delhi this week, saying he had only called for peace and progress in Bangladesh. He said he had no intention of distancing himself from Hasina or the Awami League to facilitate his return.The Rahman government, however, has rejected any suggestion of special treatment. His press secretary A.A.M. Saleh told Reuters that Shakib was facing the consequences of his association with the former government and that Bangladeshi law applied equally to everyone.“Shakib Al Hasan is an accused person, and he must surrender before the courts of Bangladesh to face the judicial process,” Saleh said.Shakib said he had previously tried to return. In late 2024, he boarded a flight home after receiving assurances that he would be protected, but was reportedly instructed to turn around while the plane was in transit. He returned to New York after landing in Dubai.A subsequent attempt also failed after he posted a birthday message for Hasina, which authorities cited as a reason for preventing his entry, he said.Despite the political and legal uncertainty, Shakib has not retired from international cricket. He said he wants to play a farewell series at home and hopes to represent Bangladesh at the 2027 ODI World Cup, although he acknowledged that he cannot continue indefinitely.“I am feeling good, still enjoying the game, playing well also,” Shakib told Reuters. “But ... age is not on my side at this moment, so I cannot wait for too long.”The cricketer also said he has not seen his parents in Bangladesh for two years and that the prolonged separation had been difficult for his family.
Article Summary: Bangladesh cricket star shakib al hasan says he is ready to return home and face trial on murder charges if the government guarantees his security. Shakib has been living in exile in the united states since former prime minister sheikh hasina was ousted in a student-led uprising in august 2024.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Arnold Schwarzenegger: "What is the point of being on this Earth if you…” - a timeless lesson on being unapologetically yourself
Article Text:
Quote of the Day by Arnold Schwarzenegger (AP photo)

T

Quote of the day by Arnold Schwarzenegger

"What is the point of being on this Earth if you are going to be like everyone else?"

What is the meaning behind the quote by Arnold Schwarzenegger

Where this quote actually comes from

Why individuality tends to drive genuine progress

Why constant comparison quietly limits people

Why real courage matters so much in choosing a different path

Why taking a real risk tends to open up real opportunity

Why authenticity tends to build steadier confidence

Why this idea clearly reaches well beyond fame

A note on Arnold Schwarzenegger's journey

Other famous quotes by Arnold Schwarzenegger

"Just remember, you can't climb the ladder of success with your hands in your pockets."

"Strength does not come from winning. Your struggles develop your strengths."

"Never follow the crowd, go where it's empty."

"The worst thing I can be is the same as everybody else. I hate that."

Why this quote continues to inspire generations

People are often taught, from a young age, to fit in quietly, follow the path already laid out, and avoid standing out too much. Arnold Schwarzenegger built his entire life pushing back against that instinct. "What is the point of being on this Earth if you are going to be like everyone else?" he asked. Born in a small Austrian village, he went on to become a champion bodybuilder, one of Hollywood's biggest stars, and eventually Governor of California, at every stage doing something people around him considered fairly unrealistic, and proving each time that unrealistic was not remotely the same thing as impossible. His story is a reminder that true success rarely comes from blending in with the crowd, but from having the courage to trust your own instincts, embrace what makes you different, and pursue goals others dismiss as impossible.hrough relentless discipline, resilience and an unwavering belief in his vision, Schwarzenegger repeatedly turned ambitious dreams into reality, inspiring millions to challenge limitations, ignore discouraging voices and recognise that extraordinary achievements often begin with the willingness to think and act differently. His remarkable journey demonstrates that persistence, calculated risk-taking and self-belief can overcome humble beginnings, transforming bold aspirations into lasting achievements while encouraging future generations to pursue their own ambitions with confidence, determination and resilience.Schwarzenegger is not simply arguing that people should act different purely to attract attention. He is making a case for originality, ambition and genuine authenticity. Every person carries a unique set of talents, experiences and perspectives, and this quote is really encouraging people to actually develop those qualities rather than spend their life copying someone else's version of success. Real fulfilment, in his framing, comes from becoming the fullest version of yourself, not an imitation of someone else's.This line appears in Total Recall: My Unbelievably True Life Story, Schwarzenegger's own 2012 memoir. Elsewhere in the same book, he gives an even more direct version of the same instinct, "Never follow the crowd, go where it's empty," a line that captures precisely the strategy he actually used throughout his career, deliberately choosing paths other people had largely avoided rather than competing directly on the same crowded ground everyone else was already fighting over, whether that meant bodybuilding, Hollywood, or eventually politics.Nearly every real breakthrough in history came from someone willing to challenge whatever everyone else already accepted as settled fact. Scientists questioned theories treated as beyond doubt. Entrepreneurs built businesses other people considered simply impossible. Genuine innovation depends almost entirely on people prepared to think differently from the crowd around them, which is exactly the spirit Schwarzenegger's quote is celebrating.Modern life makes comparing yourself to others almost unavoidable, through social media, at work, even at school. That constant comparison tends to distract people from actually discovering their own real strengths. Success becomes considerably more meaningful once it reflects genuine personal growth rather than simply outcompeting someone else. The real goal was never becoming someone else. It was becoming the fullest expression of your own actual abilities.Choosing an unconventional path is rarely easy. People question the decision. They criticise the ambition behind it. They doubt whether it will actually work. Schwarzenegger experienced every single one of these reactions directly. His accent, his physique and his unconventional background were all initially treated as disadvantages in Hollywood. Rather than trying to change who he actually was, he turned those same characteristics into a genuine part of his identity instead.Meaningful achievement usually requires stepping outside familiar territory entirely. Staying comfortable generally means staying exactly the same. Trying something genuinely new brings real uncertainty with it, but that same uncertainty is also where real possibility actually lives. Authenticity builds real confidence precisely because it removes the constant need to pretend, and people who genuinely embrace who they are tend to hold up better under criticism as a result.Schwarzenegger's message was never really limited to athletes, actors or politicians. Individuality genuinely matters in every field, not only the ones that end up in the spotlight.Schwarzenegger rose from a modest upbringing in Austria to become a seven-time Mr. Olympia champion before building an enormously successful acting career, including films such as The Terminator, Predator and True Lies. Throughout his career, he has consistently encouraged people to think boldly, set genuinely ambitious goals, and refuse to be limited by conventional expectations.Many of Schwarzenegger's best-known quotes revolve around discipline, resilience and self-belief, reflecting lessons drawn from decades of competing in bodybuilding, building a Hollywood career and later serving in public office.In a world where simply fitting in often looks easier than standing out, Schwarzenegger's quote is a reminder that real originality still holds lasting value. The greatest achievements are rarely produced through imitation. They come from people willing to follow their own actual convictions, embrace what genuinely makes them different, and contribute something the world did not already have, even when that choice looks fairly unrealistic to almost everyone else watching from the sidelines.
